subject: Audit & retention: playbook + routing review and prioritization
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Audit + retention: baseline samples + routing questions

Folks —

Attaching a first pass (audit_sample_definitions.xlsx) that Helix asked for during yesterday's call. They want us to outline:

- Which events we surface in the audit stream (admin events, token lifecycle, model routing decisions)
- Retention windows by event class and how that maps to BYOK/CMEK boundaries
- Where we route evidence (audit bucket vs. product logs vs. tenant escrow) and who owns access

Quick asks: can we confirm owners for the three columns in the sheet ("event schema", "retention tier", "routing destination") by EOD tomorrow? Helix is pushing for a short turn-around because they're bundling this into a Q4 compliance review.

Also flag: Helix asked whether we can provide a diagram showing KMS touchpoints for private deployments — I added a note to include a rough sketch.

Marissa
Product Compliance PM
Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 19 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Audit + retention: baseline samples + routing questions

Thanks Marissa — good baseline. A few clarifying points from security:

1) "Model routing decisions" — do you mean the per-request routing metadata (e.g., which model variant served the request, fallback triggers)? We should include both the routing decision and the reason code (capacity vs. degradation).

2) Retention tiers: for any tenant BYOK flows, we can't keep plaintext keys or key material in product logs — only references/timestamps. That will influence how we label "routing destination" (i.e., audit bucket should hold references + hashes, not key blobs).

3) Timeline: I'm available to review the KMS touchpoint diagram this afternoon. If Priyom can produce the initial draft of routing destinations, I can annotate security constraints.

Irene
Security Engineering

Subject: Re: Audit + retention: baseline samples + routing questions

Posting the ops constraints / proposed mapping below so the team has something concrete to triage:

Proposal (high level):
- Tier A (30d): auth/authn events, API key lifecycle, model routing decisions (reason codes), rate-limit events — route to hot audit store (searchable, 30d)
- Tier B (90d): billing-relevant logs, config changes, canary rollouts — route to warm retention (index + long-tail storage)
- Tier C (365d): long-term evidence (redacted transcripts, export snapshots) — route to escrow/tenant bucket with restricted access

Ops notes: KV cache and model cache hits are very high-volume; we should avoid routing every cache lookup to the hot audit store. Suggest we provide sampling rules for noisy signals (configurable per-tenant).

I've dropped a crude KMS touchpoint sketch as kms-integration-diagram.png. The key point: private/Tenant-BYO flows require an extra step where the control-plane stores a key-reference and the data-plane talks directly to the tenant-managed KMS for wrapping. We must not include wrapped-key payloads in any searchable audit index.

Action items I propose (owners):
- Priyom: produce routing-destination column + sampling rules (draft by Fri 8/20)
- Irene: review security constraints and produce redaction rules (by Mon 8/23)
- Marissa: consolidate and send final sample list to Helix (target Tue 8/24)

Priyom
Platform Ops

Attachment: kms-integration-diagram.png (png, 112KB)

From: secops@helix-thera.com <secops@helix-thera.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: ACME Legal <contracts@acme.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Aug 2026 16:40:00 -04:00
Subject: RE: Audit + retention: baseline samples + routing questions

Hi team — Helix SecOps here. Thanks for the quick turn. A few requirements from our side that will affect prioritization: 

- For our regulators we need a 365-day searchable index for admin actions and model selection decision traces. We can accept redacted content (pseudonymized transcripts) but need clear mapping to tenant IDs and KMS reference IDs.
- Evidence exports must be verifiable (checksums + signed manifests). Can Redwood sign manifests for escrowed snapshots?
- We will accept sampling on noisy signals but need an auditable sampling policy (how often and why).

If you can confirm whether Redwood can produce signed manifests and a configurable sampling policy by next Tuesday (8/24), we can move forward on the compliance review.

Thanks,
Helix SecOps

Thanks everyone — good points. Decision proposal for triage:

1) Scope the deliverable to three artifacts for Helix by 8/24:
   - Definitive event sample list (Marissa)
   - Routing + sampling policy (Priyom)
   - Security redaction rules + manifest signing approach (Irene)

2) For BYO/KMS we will explicitly document: no key materials in audit indexes, only key IDs and wrap/unwrap timestamps. Priyom to add a short note about the control-plane reference flow vs data-plane wrap flow.

3) Checkpoint: schedule a 30-min sync with Helix on Tue 8/24 @ 10am PT to run through the artifacts and confirm the signed-manifest ask. I'll own scheduling.

Open question for product: does this need a dedicated roadmap slot (work in Q4) or can we support Helix as a one-off compliance package? Naomi — your call on prioritization and whether engineering should reserve a sprint for integration work.

Marcus
VP, Product
Redwood Inference
